content:
Alongside the ongoing all-time low on the 4-pack of Apple’s latest AirTag 2, today’s 9to5Toys Lunch Break is headlined by Amazon still offering Apple’s AirPods 4 at nearly 25% off ahead of July 4th and the pre-price hike M5 iPad Pro deals still live at up to $350 off. We also have the most affordable 13-inch M4 iPad Air at $200 off and the rest of the official Apple 4th of July accessory deals from $15 – AirTag 2, Magic Keyboard, Magic Mouse, iPhone cases, Sport Band, and more. Head below for a closer look at those and more.

Apple’s 2026, next-generation AirTag saw its first notable discounts for Prime Day this year. The listing for the single AirTag 2 has already started to jump back up in price, and we are about to turn the page on June 2026, there’s a good chance the 4-pack might too – it is still down at its lowest price ever as of the time of writing.

The single has jumped to $27, but Amazon is still offering the 4-pack of Apple’s latest AirTag 2 trackers down at $89 shipped.

Amazon still offering Apple’s AirPods 4 at nearly 25% off ahead of July 4th

While the AirPods Pro 3 price has jumped back up, as expected, Amazon is still offering Apple’s most affordable current-gen AirPods 4 down at the same $99 we tracked for Prime Day ahead of the July 4th celebrations.

Amazon is now offering AirPods 4 down at $99 shipped. Regularly $129, this is nearly 25% off the list price and on par with the best prices we have tracked across all of 2026, outside of a brief dip for less than an hour back in early March.

While we have tracked this same deal a number of times this year, with Prime Day bumping right up next to the 4th of July sales this year we wanted to make sure this one was on the radar this week for those looking towards a summer refresh – there is a chance Amazon bumps the price back up this weekend once the competitor July 4th sales wrap up (although Best Buy is charging full price right now, despite being in the midst of its July 4th sale).

You’re looking at Apple’s most affordable set of earbuds here, complete with Personalized Spatial Audio, what and water resistance, the USB-C charging case, up to 30 hours of battery life, and more, all powered by its H2 chip.

These are the pre-price hike M5 iPad Pro deals still live at up to $350 off (Jumping up in price quick now)

All but a few of the current-generation Apple releases that just received price hikes are still sitting down at pre-price increase deals. This 1TB 11-inch M5 iPad Pro happens to be one of them (among a few others down below) – you can land it at $350 off the new list.

Amazon is offering this 1TB 11-inch M5 iPad Pro down at $1,449.99 shipped.

Previously a $1,599 machine, it now fetches $1,799 at Apple and Amazon is also reflecting the new regular price. It is, however, still sitting down at the Prime Day pre-price hike deal with just shy of $350 off the new list.

This deal, much like loads of others we have highlighted for folks over the last 5 days or so, is surely going to jump in price significantly and likely sooner than later.

While the 11-inch model featured above is a real standout here, there are a few other M5 iPad Pro configs still sitting at notable pre-price hike rates at the moment:

M5 iPad Pro 11-inch:

  • 11-inch M5 iPad Pro 256GB $949 (Now Reg. $1,199)
  • 11-inch M5 iPad Pro 1TB $1,449 (Now Reg. $1,799)
  • 11-inch M5 iPad Pro 2TB $1,949 (Now Reg. $2,299)

M5 iPad Pro 13-inch:

  • 13-inch M5 iPad Pro 256GB $1,199 (Now Reg. $1,499)
  • 13-inch M5 iPad Pro 1TB $1,749 (Now Reg. $2,099)
  • 13-inch M5 iPad Pro 2TB $2,249 (Now Reg. $2,599)

Most affordable 13-inch M4 iPad Air is $200 off at Amazon, more

The latest M4 iPad Air just saw a sizable official price hike, as you likely know by now, but you can still land the most affordable 13-inch model at $200 off right now.

Amazon is offering the 128GB 13-inch M4 iPad Air at $749 shipped. Regularly $949 these days, this is a straight up $200 off the list price and a notable discount for one of the more affordable models in the lineup.

This deal is live on all four colors as of the time of writing: Blue, Gray, Purple, and Starlight.

While we have seen this machine down in the $700 range in the past, the price is much higher now and grabbing one at $200 off is quite notable.

The iPad Air lineup’s discounts tend to be much more modest for the most part until we get much closer to, or after the, next-generation launches. Catching the entry and most affordable model at $200 off the list price is rare at best, and there’s no telling where the price might land on this model in the coming days, weeks, and months.

Here’s a look at how pricing lands across the lineup ahead of July 4th – to all models are back in stock after the price hikes, but you can still land some great deals on the entry variants and as much as $250 off the 1TB:
